name: Saudi Public Investment Fund

summary.text: The Public Investment Fund (PIF) is the sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia. Its board is chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and its governor is Yasir Al-Rumayyan. PIF reported assets under management of over $900 billion at the end of 2025. It committed up to $45 billion to the SoftBank Vision Fund in 2017, invested $3.5 billion in Uber in 2016 with a board seat for Al-Rumayyan, is the majority owner of electric-vehicle maker Lucid, and in May 2025 launched the AI company Humain.

facts.claim: PIF's board is chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Yasir Al-Rumayyan serves as governor, running day-to-day strategy; Al-Rumayyan concurrently chairs Saudi Aramco and Newcastle United.
facts.quote: chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, with Yasir Al-Rumayyan serving as Governor

facts.claim: PIF's 2025 annual report states that the fund had over $900 billion in assets under management and more than doubled net profit year on year; the Saudi Press Agency reported AUM exceeding SAR 3.4 trillion at the end of 2025.
facts.quote: over $900 billion in assets under management

facts.claim: In May 2017 PIF signed a binding agreement to invest up to $45 billion over five years in the SoftBank Vision Fund, building on an October 2016 memorandum of understanding, as the fund's largest outside backer.
facts.quote: PIF will invest up to $45 billion in the Vision Fund over the next five years.

sources.title: The Public Investment Fund, SoftBank Group and Mubadala joined by initial investors in Vision Fund including Apple, Foxconn, Qualcomm and Sharp

facts.claim: In June 2016 PIF invested $3.5 billion in Uber as part of Uber's Series G round at a $62.5 billion valuation, one of its largest international transactions at the time, and PIF managing director Yasir Al-Rumayyan joined Uber's board as part of the agreement.
facts.quote: The investment, part of Uber's Series G fundraising round, is one of PIF's single largest international transactions to date.

facts.claim: PIF, through its affiliate Ayar Third Investment Company, is the majority shareholder of Lucid Group, holding about 57 percent of common stock as of April 2026 and having provided a further $1.5 billion in funding in August 2024; under an investor rights agreement Ayar can nominate five directors while it owns at least half the stock.
facts.quote: the fund's combined holdings reached 280,992,324 shares, or about 56.85% of Lucid's common stock, according to securities filings

facts.claim: In May 2025 PIF launched Humain, a company intended to operate across the AI value chain, including data centers, cloud services and models, with Tareq Amin as CEO. During a Riyadh forum that month, Nvidia agreed to supply Humain with chips for up to 500 megawatts of AI data centers, and AMD announced a collaboration of up to $10 billion for 500 megawatts of capacity.
facts.quote: AMD and Humain announced a collaboration of up to $10 billion to deploy 500 MW of AI compute capacity over five years.
